reasoning: 1. TARGET ENGAGEMENT: Strong evidence of target engagement - lovastatin significantly reduced cholesterol (-27.25 mg/dL) and LDL (-25.28 mg/dL), confirming HMG-CoA reductase inhibition. 2. PATHWAY MODULATION: Mixed evidence of downstream pathway effects. Some biomarkers moved in expected directions (e-cadherin decreased in placebo vs increased in treatment, n-cadherin decreased in placebo vs increased in treatment), but others showed minimal changes (Ki-67, p21, HIF1alpha). The mevalonate pathway modulation appears partial. 3. CLINICAL TRANSLATION: Primary endpoint failed - histopathologic regression of atypical nevi did not occur. Effect sizes were modest (0.5 vs -0.12 for pathologist 1, 0.17 vs 0.04 for pathologist 2) but no statistical significance reported. 4. POPULATION EFFECTS: Some population-level benefit observed - fewer patients had increased nevi count with lovastatin (1 vs 7 with placebo), suggesting the mechanism may work in a subset. 5. CONFOUNDERS: No major confounders identified. Study was adequately powered (n=80), duration was reasonable (24 weeks), and safety was acceptable.

failure_modes.evidence: Target was clearly engaged (cholesterol/LDL reduction), some downstream biomarkers moved (e-cadherin, n-cadherin), but primary histopathologic regression endpoint failed to show benefit
